senses.gloss: m. nom. gent. of Tarsus, Tarsian.—Pl. טַרְסִיִּים, טוּרְ׳.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 7a">Meg. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>בגתן</he> … <he>שני ט׳ היו והיו מספרים בלשון טרסי</he> Ms. M. (only <he>בגתן … שני טרשיים היו</he>) Bigthan and Teresh were two Tarsians and conversed in the Tarsian language; <cite ref="Megillah 13b:10">ib. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>שני ט׳ … טורסי</he> (Ms. M. … <he>תרסיים תרסי</he>).

<cite ref="Megillah 26a:8">Ib. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>בה״כ של ט׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>טור׳</he>; <cite ref="Tosefta Megillah 3:6">Tosef. ib. III</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Megillah 2:6">II</cite>), 6 <he>אלכסנדרים</he>) the synagogue of the Tarsians in Jerusalem (Rashi: of the bronze-workers, v. <cite ref="I00849">preced.</cite>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 2:5:4">Y. Shek. II, 47ᵃ</cite> <he>בה״כ של ט׳</he> (<cite ref="Yevamot 96b">Yeb. 96ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="I00088"><he>טבריא</he></cite>).
